source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #352 (branch fix/334-borrowed-drop at head 94013a772f0a27e912410f8791a36ca48c8812fb — the #334 change (a borrow of an owned resource can no longer be dropped while the borrow is outstanding, and ownership transfer of a borrowed resource is rejected), as revised by the third Codex review round (the handle-transfer walk resolves every borrow’s record in a first pass, before any own moves its source entry, so a borrow passed after an own of the same resource is no longer silently dropped) on top of current main b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b (PR #353), which has not moved since the branch’s second re-baseline; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45604869761 and 45604878403 against the branch and pull-request run 45603860686, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #352 (#334, a borrow of an owned resource can no longer be dropped while the borrow is outstanding, and ownership transfer of a borrowed resource is rejected), the branch’s third: the third Codex review round found that the handle-transfer walk processed arguments in order, so when a call passed the same resource as (own R, borrow R), the own’s transfer removed the source entry before the borrow was looked up; the borrow’s identity was then never reported, and the destination could destroy the resource while it was borrowed. The walk now resolves every borrow’s record in a first pass, before any own moves, and the second pass consumes those records, so the protection no longer depends on parameter or field order. Main has not moved since the branch’s second re-baseline (main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b, PR #353), so no merge was needed, and the pull-request run on the new head tripped the gate on the twelve series of the three configurations that link telomere-component. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45604888709, 45604898651 and 45604915383 on main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b; all three runs pass the gate against main’s checked-in baseline). This PR’s delta against the main control is confined to the same 12 series: in release, stripped file +11,776 B (component), +11,776 B (wasi) and +11,760 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +10,576 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +7,160 B / +7,176 B / +7,192 B and stripped .text +5,808 B / +5,824 B / +5,824 B. The third round’s own increment over the previous baseline is, in release, stripped file +2,360 B / +2,376 B / +2,360 B and stripped .text +1,856 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +864 B / +880 B / +880 B and stripped .text +768 B / +784 B / +784 B. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. All twelve series exceed the checked-in baseline, so those twelve are re-baselined to the branch measurements. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +11.50% (2,433,656 B to 2,713,632 B), up from +11.41%; the release core-nosimd stripped file series is unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
